$description: Canonical elevation source. Hand-edit this file only; dist/ is generated.

meta.note: Three levels in use. Each is a Tailwind shadow (sm or md) with a 1px hairline ring in front of it. The ring is the part that carries the system's look: surfaces are defined by a crisp edge, with the drop shadow doing very little. Only the card ring changes between themes - near-black at 5% in light, near-white at 10% in dark. The drops are identical in both.

none.usage: Inputs, textareas and other controls that sit flush in a surface. The reference gives these no shadow at all - they are distinguished by their fill, not by lift.

card.usage: Every card and panel. The only theme-varying elevation: its hairline ring flips from near-black 5% to near-white 10%, because a dark surface needs a light edge to read as raised.

thumb.usage: The knob of a switch. Same drops as card, with no ring - it sits on a coloured track, where a hairline would read as a seam.

raised.usage: Slider thumbs in the reference. The only level that reads as genuinely floating, so it is also the right choice for popovers, dropdowns and tooltips - which the reference never shows in an elevated state.

notes.ringVsBorder: The 1px ring is part of the shadow, not a CSS border. That keeps it outside the box model, so it never shifts layout. Do not reimplement it as a border unless the platform forces you to - Compose does.
notes.tailwindBase: card and thumb use Tailwind's shadow-sm drops; raised uses shadow-md. Both exactly.
